cards.explanation: The answer is Their Savior. God said, “They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal.” Then the verse says, “So He became their Savior.” The next verse tells us how He did it: “In His love and compassion He redeemed them…” That's a whole lot of rescuing, friends.

The answer is False. The prayer says, “In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them.” He didn't keep His distance. He was hurting right along with them. Friends, that is a close God.

The answer is enemy. The prayer says Israel “…rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit. So He turned and became their enemy, and He Himself fought against them.” I think that's one of the heaviest lines in the whole prayer. It's good to know it's in there, because the prayer doesn't hide it.

The answer is the sea. The people remember and ask, “Where is He who brought them through the sea with the shepherds of His flock?” They're looking back at the days of Moses, Israel's leader. A few verses later it says He “…divided the waters before them…” You don't forget a walk like that, friends.

The answer is to make His name famous forever. The prayer says He “…divided the waters before them to gain for Himself everlasting renown…” Renown means a name people know. That's the reason the prayer gives, friends.

The answer is False. The verse says He led them “…through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble?” They did not stumble, so the part about stumbling the whole way doesn't hold, friends.

The answer is that it is being held back. The prayer says, “Your yearning and compassion for me are restrained.” Notice the one praying isn't pretending everything is fine. They say how it feels and ask God to look down and see. I think honest prayers like that are the best kind.

The answer is Father, friends. The prayer says, “Yet You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us.” Then it says it again: “You, O LORD, are our Father…” Abraham does not know them, and Israel does not acknowledge them. Still, the prayer holds on to that name.

The answer is Return to them. The prayer says, “Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your heritage.” That comes right after the hard questions. They don't just ask why, friends. They ask Him to come back.

The answer is True, friends. The prayer says, “For a short while Your people possessed Your holy place, but our enemies have trampled Your sanctuary.” I think this part is a hard thing to say out loud, and the prayer says it anyway.

The answer is His enemies. The prayer asks God to come down “…to make Your name known to Your enemies, so that the nations will tremble at Your presence!” The picture is fire making water boil. Water that's been sitting calm starts bubbling, and everybody notices.

The answer is True. The prayer says, “From ancient times no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides You, who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him.” Nobody ever heard of another God like that, never mind saw one, friends. And the LORD acts for those who wait.

The answer is that they ask how they can be saved if they stay in their sins. Right after “Surely You were angry, for we sinned.” the prayer asks, “How can we be saved if we remain in our sins?” They don't make excuses, friends. They just ask the honest question.

The answer is False. The prayer says, “…all our righteous acts are like filthy rags…” It also says, “Each of us has become like something unclean…” Those are the pictures it uses, friends, not clean ones.

The answer is that He hid it from them. The prayer says, “No one calls on Your name or strives to take hold of You. For You have hidden Your face from us and delivered us into the hand of our iniquity.” It's a sad verse, and I think it's meant to be. They say it plainly.

The answer is potter, friends. The verse says, “we are the clay, and You are the potter; we are all the work of Your hand.” I'm a stamper, so I know a little about pressing shapes into soft stuff. But a potter's hands shape the whole thing, and that's the picture here.

The answer is iniquity. The prayer says, “Do not be angry, O LORD, beyond measure; do not remember our iniquity forever.” Iniquity means sin. They name it out loud and ask for mercy, friends, and they don't try to hide it.

The answer is that it was burned with fire. The prayer says, “Our holy and beautiful temple, where our fathers praised You, has been burned with fire, and all that was dear to us lies in ruins.” I think this one hurts. It's a hard line, friends, and the prayer says it plainly.

The answer is True. The prayer ends with questions: “After all this, O LORD, will You restrain Yourself? Will You keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?” It doesn't wrap up neat, friends. It ends with the people still asking God directly.
